recentItems.title: LIVE: What Is the WorldSkills Competition All About?
recentItems.description:
The highly anticipated 48th WorldSkills Competition is about to take place in Shanghai. Skills competitors from around the world will gather along the Huangpu River, pursuing their dreams through craftsmanship and showcasing the brilliance of technical skills in the new era.

From September 16 to 18, Audrey will take you on an exploration of the WorldSkills Museum—the only museum in the world dedicated to skills. Here you will learn about the century-long history of the WorldSkills Competition. Together with Serbian video blogger Filip, you will experience the craftsmanship behind China’s intangible cultural heritage, and join Iraqi video blogger Al Kalthoom Aya in trying out WorldSkills competition disciplines.

Tune in to the livestream and discover the beauty of skills.

recentItems.title: Pop Mart's Beijing Theme Park Draws Crowds with Immersive Upgrades
recentItems.description:
Beijing's Pop Land, fresh from a new round of renovations, continues drawing crowds this summer.

All year, the amusement park has been refreshing and unlocking its features, transforming the park from one that mainly catered to photo-check-ins, into one with more immersive experiences and attractions.

New scenes, characters and new rides thrill visitors of all ages, and nationalities. The Pop Land performance director says they've doubled the number of shows since the park opened a few years ago.

Since the beginning of this year, Pop Land has optimized visitor flow routes and increased the frequency of character appearances, raising the chance of visitors encountering IP characters by nearly 30 percent.

recentItems.title: China Weaves Integrated Import Network across Sea, Land, Air
recentItems.description:
China's multi dimensional trading network including sea, land and air transport, has made it possible for the country to increase its imports in the first half of the year, data shows.

From January to July this year, China's goods imports reached about 1.8 trillion U.S. dollars, a 22 percent year-on-year increase -- eight percentage points higher than the country’s export growth from the same period.

As the world's largest goods trader, China relies on maritime transport for over 90 percent of its cross-border trade. Eight of the world's top ten ports by cargo throughput are in China.

China's land routes are also expanding. The China Europe Railway Express reaches 236 cities in 26 European countries and over 100 cities in 11 Asian countries.

And air cargo networks are also growing. This year, China opened 103 new international air cargo routes, adding 229 round-trip flights per week.

China has been the world's second largest import market for 17 consecutive years, with imports growing at an average annual rate of 5.1 percent.
